_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Measuring, diagnosing, budgeting, and improving performance — latency, throughput, Core Web Vitals, database queries,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "profile this slow dashboard and decide what to optimize first"
cases.context: The agent has access to the performance-engineering skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is performance-engineering the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes performance-engineering as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against api-design, entity-relationship-modeling, refactor
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the performance-engineering workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore performance-engineering
Does not route to api-design, entity-relationship-modeling, refactor when the performance-engineering scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
